Action Plan:
1. Provide patient with NHS self-referral link for talking therapy (CBT) and additional trusted online resources for anxiety management and sleep hygiene; patient agrees to engage.
2. Arrange basic blood tests (FBC, TFTs, U&Es, glucose, iron studies ± B₁₂/folate) via support line to screen for metabolic/thyroid causes of palpitations; schedule GP follow-up 1 week after results available.
3. Advise patient to phone GP sooner if anxiety or palpitations escalate, if work becomes unmanageable, or if any suicidal thoughts emerge; medication for anxiety may be considered at that stage.
4. Document sleep-hygiene advice in patient notes for her reference.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
6. (If asked at follow-up) A COVID-19 vaccine suitability assessment was performed. The patient is eligible for a government-funded vaccine and their response to the vaccination advice is documented.

Subjective:
• 28-year-old female presents with 2 months of worsening anxiety since starting a new, stressful retail head-office job.  
• Symptoms: daily morning dread of leaving house, irregular rapid heartbeat episodes (up to 10 min), shallow sleep 3–4 h/night, low energy, loss of enjoyment in running, tennis, socialising.  
• No previous similar episodes; no panic attacks or suicidal thoughts.  
• Past medical history: none reported.  
• Family history: mother with depression.  
• Medications: none.  
• Allergies: not documented.  
• Social: lives with parents; alcohol—binges Fri/Sat, occasional weekday wine (exact units not tracked); occasional smoking; no recreational drugs.

Objective:
• Video consult—no physical exam performed.  
• Mental state: appears distressed, anxious, low affect (qualitative observation only).  
• Vitals, weight, cardiovascular exam: not performed.

Investigations/results: none to date.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Anxiety related to new job (Adjustment disorder with anxiety / evolving Generalised Anxiety Disorder):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Adjustment disorder with anxiety (DDx item: “Adjustment disorder with anxiety (early GAD)” – High likelihood).
   - Differential diagnosis: Major depressive disorder (Medium), Generalised Anxiety Disorder (progression), work-related stress (DDx “T”).
   - Investigations: none specific; screen questionnaires possible (GAD-7) at follow-up.
   - Treatment: Self-referral to IAPT talking therapy; provide online CBT/anxiety resources; monitor severity; consider pharmacotherapy (e.g., SSRI) if no improvement or deterioration.
   - Referrals: IAPT service (patient to self-refer).

2. Palpitations:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Anxiety-related palpitations.
   - Differential diagnosis: Hyperthyroidism (DDx – Low–Medium), supraventricular tachycardia/arrhythmia (Low), iron-deficiency anaemia (Low), caffeine/alcohol-induced palpitations (DDx “I2”).
   - Investigations: Basic bloods (FBC, TFTs, U&Es, glucose, iron studies); consider ECG if palpitations worsen or bloods abnormal.
   - Treatment: Reassure; manage underlying anxiety.
   - Referrals: GP follow-up after results; cardiology referral only if arrhythmia suspected.

3. Insomnia:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Secondary to anxiety.
   - Differential diagnosis: Primary insomnia, hyperthyroidism, alcohol-related sleep disturbance.
   - Investigations: none separate (covered above).
   - Treatment: Provide written sleep-hygiene guidance; CBT-I principles via online resources.
   - Referrals: Included in talking therapy.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: formal allergy status, complete medication reconciliation, vital signs, menstrual history (for anaemia screen), caffeine intake, mood/anxiety screening scores.  
● No internal transcript–DDx conflicts identified.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; minor background noise, no inaudible sections.
